detail: supported
Training struggles when the target object shape differs drastically from the source object [S1].

The claim states that training struggles when the target object shape differs drastically from the source object. The provided notes explicitly list 'Training struggles when the target object shape drastically differs from the source object, leading to incomplete edits.' Furthermore, the passage text confirms this by stating, 'we find that in some cases, especially the new object shape is hugely different from the old one, the training process will be very tough for the model.' Both the notes and the passage directly support the claim.
supported
The method is both time and memory intensive [S1].

The claim states that the method is time and memory intensive. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states in the 'Limitations' section that 'the whole process is time-consuming and space-consuming' (where space-consuming refers to memory) and notes that it 'takes more than 30 minutes to generate a relatively high-quality 3D model'. This directly supports the claim.
supported
Objects generated at the periphery may incorrectly combine features from multiple source objects, whereas central regions remain consistent [S1].

The claim states that objects generated at the periphery may incorrectly combine features from multiple source objects, whereas central regions remain consistent. Source [S1] explicitly mentions in its notes and the main text that 'generated objects at the periphery may incorrectly combine features from multiple source objects' and provides an example where 'the generated daisy on the edge of the view is actually combined by two orchids, while the generated daisy in the central location is much more normal.' This directly supports every part of the claim.
unsupported
It distinguishes these failure modes from the core optimization mechanics detailed in [RePaint-NeRF](14365-repaint-nerf.md) [S1].

The claim states that the evidence distinguishes these failure modes from the 'core optimization mechanics detailed in [RePaint-NeRF]'. However, the provided evidence (Source [S1]) only lists the limitations of its own method (time/memory intensity, shape difference struggles, and angle constraints). It does not mention 'RePaint-NeRF', nor does it compare its failure modes to the optimization mechanics of any other specific method. Therefore, the specific comparison claimed in the statement is not present in the evidence.
supported
In such cases, the edit may be incomplete, failing to fully replace the original geometry [S1].

The claim states that edits may be incomplete, failing to fully replace original geometry. Source [S1] explicitly mentions in the 'Limitations' section that when the new object shape is hugely different from the old one, 'the training process will be very tough for the model' and provides an example where 'the cup from the hotdog is not completely changed.' This directly supports the claim that edits can be incomplete and fail to fully replace the original geometry.
supported
Generating a high-quality 3D model at the object level requires more than 30 minutes of optimization [S1].

The claim states that generating a high-quality 3D model at the object level requires more than 30 minutes of optimization. Source [S1] explicitly states in the 'Limitations' section: 'it still takes more than 30 minutes to generate a relatively highquality 3D model at the object level.' This directly supports the claim.
supported
Restricted view angles cause geometric artifacts at image edges during optimization [S1].

The claim states that restricted view angles cause geometric artifacts at image edges during optimization. Source [S1] explicitly notes in its bullet points that 'Restricted view angles cause geometric artifacts at image edges' and explains that 'generated objects at the periphery may incorrectly combine features from multiple source objects.' The passage further supports this by describing an example where a daisy on the edge of the view is combined from two orchids, unlike the normal daisy in the center. Thus, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
supported

This article documents the empirical limitations of the RePaint-NeRF method [S1], specifically regarding computational efficiency, geometric fidelity under significant shape changes, and view-angle consistency.

The claim accurately reflects the limitations described in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states the method is 'time-consuming and space-consuming' (supporting 'computational efficiency'), notes that training is 'tough' when the 'new object shape is hugely different' (supporting 'geometric fidelity under significant shape changes'), and mentions that 'angle constraint will influence the shape' causing artifacts at the edges (supporting 'view-angle consistency').
supported
RePaint-NeRF was introduced in [S1] to enable NeRF editing via semantic masks and diffusion model guidance.

The claim states that RePaint-NeRF was introduced in [S1] to enable NeRF editing via semantic masks and diffusion model guidance. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states in the Conclusion section: 'we proposed a NeRF editing framework based on the pre-trained 2D diffusion model guidance' and mentions obtaining the edited scene by 'regenerating the masked part' and using 'depth information as supervision in the semantic mask acquisition part'. This confirms that the method uses diffusion model guidance and semantic masks for NeRF editing, and the source is identified as [S1].
supported
Due to these resource demands, the method cannot scale to larger resolutions or larger scenes [S1].

The claim states that the method cannot scale to larger resolutions or larger scenes due to resource demands. Source [S1] explicitly states in the 'Limitations' section: 'The first and most obvious problem with our method is that the whole process is time-consuming and space-consuming. For this reason, we cannot extend to a larger resolution of data or a larger scene.' This directly supports the claim.
supported

The limitations described herein were identified during the evaluation of this framework, which uses gradient guidance from a pre-trained 2D diffusion model to regenerate masked parts of the scene [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the content of the provided evidence. The evidence (Source [S1]) explicitly states in the Conclusion that the method uses a 'pre-trained 2D diffusion model guidance' and regenerates the 'masked part' via 'gradient guidance'. Furthermore, the Limitations section details that these limitations were identified during the evaluation of this specific framework, noting issues with time/memory intensity (>30 minutes), struggles with drastic shape changes, and geometric artifacts due to restricted view angles.
